dedupe_keys.name: emrald event modeling risk assessment using linked diagrams idaho national laboratory

description: EMRALD, Event Modeling Risk Assessment using Linked Diagrams, is a dynamic probabilistic risk assessment tool developed at Idaho National Laboratory. The README read on 2026-09-26 says it keeps the structure of traditional PRA, with basic events, fault trees and event trees captured inside a dynamic framework of state diagrams, offers a user interface for modelling and visualising interactions, couples one way with physics simulations and two way with customisable applications, and reports the sequence and timing of events that lead to each outcome. Coverage is generic to engineered systems and has no country scope. Access is through the GitHub source, built on .NET 6 in Visual Studio 2022 with a website for building models, a desktop application for running simulations and a documentation project. The code is free under the MIT licence. Caveats: the emrald.inl.gov site refused automated requests on the day, so only the repository was read, and setup is oriented to Windows and Visual Studio. Simulation uses are dynamic risk and cascading failure analysis of plant systems, where timing and component states matter, and resilience studies that couple risk models with physics codes. Related records: platform-openpra is an open PRA platform, and model-raven is INL's framework for driving simulation codes in risk studies.
